turns.text: Today we're comparing single-pass RAG with agentic RAG. Why might an agent help?
I think agentic RAG helps mainly because the agent can rewrite a vague question before retrieving, so for multi-hop questions it pulls the second document a single-pass retriever would miss.
Isn't RAG basically the same as fine-tuning the model on the documents?
Good question. Can someone build on Alex's point about cost?
Building on that, the cost is latency, every extra retrieval round adds a model call, so you'd cap the retries.

documents.title: Week 10 notes: Agentic RAG
documents.source: IS469 demo course notes (authored for the ClassPart AI demo)

passages.text: Single-pass retrieval-augmented generation retrieves once using the user's question and then generates an answer. It struggles when the question is vague or when the answer needs facts from more than one document.

Agentic RAG lets the model decide when and what to retrieve. Typical strategies are query rewriting, where a vague question is reformulated before retrieval, multi-hop retrieval, where a second search uses facts found in the first, and self-checking of retrieved evidence.
Each extra retrieval round adds a model call, so agentic RAG increases latency and cost. Systems usually cap the number of retrieval rounds or tool calls with a budget.
Self-RAG trains the model to grade its own retrieved passages for relevance and to critique whether its answer is supported by them.

documents.title: Week 5 notes: Fine-tuning versus retrieval
documents.source: IS469 demo course notes (authored for the ClassPart AI demo)

passages.text: Fine-tuning changes a model's weights using training examples. Retrieval-augmented generation leaves the weights unchanged and supplies documents in the prompt at inference time, so knowledge can be updated without retraining.
